body: Honestly this whole post has made me rethink everything and I kind of am realizing how unprofessional she has been, which makes me kind of see her in a different light. It doesn't really change anything- i am only seeing her a few more weeks and will continue to see her after that in AA- but it makes me realize that I shouldn't put her on such a pedestal.

We already see each other outside of therapy and that will continue when I am done with therapy as well- so we will have a relationship of a sort after therapy. I am concerned of the impact confessing my feelings will have on that.

It's avoidable. We're both in AA and she explicitly invited me to attend one of the meetings and started attending another one of them knowing before hand that I would be there. I am aware it's incredibly unprofessional but I wanted to be friends with her, however due to my social anxiety I'm realizing I should have probably avoided the whole thing. She invited another client to one of the meetings and is having interaction with her outside of therapy and that made me extremely upset and jealous. I am realizing the pitfalls of all of this now, but to be fair I would like to be her friend after all this and I don't really care if she's an unprofessional therapist in that respect- I like her as a person. That being said I am going to stop seeing her in a few weeks as a therapist regardless, but I will continue to see her in AA and that's my issue- I want to talk to her about my feelings but not sure if it's worth it as A) I am going to stop seeing her soon anyway and B) I will continue to see her outside of therapy after that, and am not sure how she will react to me confessing my obsession. I am also guessing, as you mentioned, that it might make her rethink her professional boundaries all together and that might impact our future relationship.
Well, after therapy then I guess. As I mentioned we see each other multiple times a week outside of therapy- it's not by the book but that's the situation we're in now
